questions.stem: Which statement best describes why living organisms need food?

options.text: Food provides both energy and materials needed for growth and maintenance.
Food is only required when organisms are active.
Food is not necessary if an organism is not growing.
Food is only needed to provide energy for activities.

questions.source_quote: We also need materials from outside in order to grow, develop, synthesise protein and other substances needed in the body. This source of energy and materials is the food we eat.
questions.explanation: The quote shows that food provides both energy and materials, not just energy.

questions.stem: What do autotrophs require from outside to perform photosynthesis?

options.text: Carbon dioxide and water
No materials from outside
Only sunlight
Only oxygen and water

questions.source_quote: This material is taken in the form of carbon dioxide and water which is converted into carbohydrates in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll.
questions.explanation: The quote states that autotrophs take in carbon dioxide and water from outside for photosynthesis.

questions.stem: What is the function of stomata in leaves during photosynthesis?

options.text: They absorb sunlight for the plant.
They store chlorophyll for the plant.
They are always open to let water escape.
They allow exchange of gases needed for photosynthesis.

questions.source_quote: Massive amounts of gaseous exchange takes place in the leaves through these pores for the purpose of photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: The quote explains that stomata are involved in gas exchange for photosynthesis.

questions.stem: What is the role of saliva in the digestion of food in the mouth?

options.text: It only wets the food and does not help in digestion.
It contains an enzyme that breaks down starch into simple sugar.
It absorbs nutrients directly into the blood.
It digests proteins into amino acids.

questions.source_quote: The saliva contains an enzyme called salivary amylase that breaks down starch which is a complex molecule to give simple sugar.
questions.explanation: The quote shows that saliva helps digest starch, not just wet food.

questions.stem: What is the main function of villi in the small intestine?

options.text: They absorb nutrients mainly in the stomach.
They are where most protein digestion occurs.
They secrete acid to digest food.
They increase the surface area for absorption of digested food.

questions.source_quote: The inner lining of the small intestine has numerous finger-like projections called villi which increase the surface area for absorption.
questions.explanation: The quote states that villi increase surface area for absorption in the small intestine.
